children: Floor & Decor Holdings cut its outlook for the year, despite reporting revenue growth and a higher profit in the third quarter.

The company now expects adjusted earnings in a range of $1.88 to $1.98 a share, lowering the top end of the range from $2.13. Analysts polled by FactSet currently expect full-year earnings of $1.96 a share.
It guided for net sales of between $4.765 billion and $4.835 billion, down from previous guidance in a range of $4.77 billion and $4.99 billion. Analysts are expecting $4.85 billion.

Comparable sales are expected to fall by 2% to 3.5% for the year. The company had previously said comparable sales would be in a range of flat to a 4% decline, and analysts are expecting a 2.2% decline.
In the third quarter, the company reported a profit of $64.8 million, or 61 cents a share, compared with a profit of $57.3 million, or 53 cents a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out certain one-time items, adjusted earnings came in at 61 cents a share. Analysts polled by FactSet were expecting 57 cents a share.
Net sales rose to $1.21 billion from $1.18 billion a year prior. Analysts had been expecting $1.22 billion.
Comparable sales fell 1.4% during the quarter, in line with analyst expectations.
Floor and Decor also said Thursday that its executive board chair, Thomas Taylor, is transitioning to the role of board chair.
Taylor said the transition reflects the execution of the company's succession plan to Chief Executive Brad Paulsen, who succeeded Taylor as CEO in December.

The company also said that it appointed Lauren Taylor Wolfe, a co-founder and managing partner of Impactive Capital, as a new independent director, effective in February.Lead independent director Norman Axelrod will not stand for reelection at the company's 2027 shareholder meeting, the company added.
